Merge Matching Sub-lists of val Against x

Source: R/RcppExports.R
modify_list2.Rd

For every element of val, if x has an element with the same name and both are lists, the two are merged recursively with modify_list(); otherwise the element of val is used unchanged.

Usage

modify_list2(x, val)

Arguments

x

A list. Provides the base values for matching sub-lists.

val

A list. Provides the new values.

Value

A list with the same length and names as val.

Details

Note that the result is built from val only: its length and names are those of val, and elements of x whose names do not appear in val are not carried over. This differs from utils::modifyList().

  • Names are matched exactly (case-sensitive). If x has duplicated names, the first match is used.

  • Elements of val that are unnamed, have an NA name or an empty name are passed through unchanged.

  • Unmodified elements are shared with the inputs, not deep-copied.

  • Only the names attribute of val is kept on the result.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- list(
  a = list(p = 1, q = 2),
  b = 1,
  c = list(z = 0)
)
val <- list(
  a = list(q = 20, r = 30), # both lists: merged recursively
  b = list(new = TRUE),     # `x$b` is not a list: replaced by `val$b`
  d = 4                     # not in `x`: kept as is
)

res <- SigBridgeR:::modify_list2(x, val)
str(res)
# res$a: p = 1, q = 20, r = 30
# res$b: list(new = TRUE)
# res$d: 4
# `x$c` is not in `val`, so it is not in the result
names(res)

# unnamed elements are passed through
SigBridgeR:::modify_list2(list(1), list(list(a = 1), 2))

# non-list inputs are rejected
try(SigBridgeR:::modify_list2(1:3, list()))
} # }
